`CommGrpCat.{u}`, datum typed as in `JacobianData.rep` (design §5). -/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory AlgebraicGeometry

section DryRun

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
variable (F : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u})
variable (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))

/-- The exact discharge shape of the frozen `instGrpObj` (datum-flow table §4.6, row 2). -/
noncomputable def dryRunGrpObj : GrpObj J :=
  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy J (F ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) rep

/-- The unit formula the `comp_ofCurve` row relies on: `η[J]` is the rep-image of `1`. -/
example :
    letI : GrpObj J := dryRunGrpObj F J rep
    η[J] = rep.homEquiv.symm 1 := by

/-- `uniqueUpToIso` (baseChangeIso row): two data for the same functor give an iso. -/

    (J' : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep' : ((F ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J') :
    J ≅ J' :=
  rep.uniqueUpToIso rep'

/-- The `Grp`-bundled object of the functor row: `.mk J` with the derived instance. -/
noncomputable def dryRunGrpMk : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))) :=
  letI : GrpObj J := dryRunGrpObj F J rep
  .mk J

end DryRun

1160	\section{The projective line: inputs for the finiteness argument}
1161	
1162	This section collects the facts about \(\PP^1\) and about morphisms over \(\Spec k\) that
1163	the finiteness argument of the next section consumes. It builds on the description of
1164	\(\PP^1\), its standard charts \(U_0, U_1\), the chart coordinates
1165	\(t_{ij} = X_j/X_i \in A_{(X_i)}\), and the section-ring identifications
1166	\(\gamma_0, \gamma_1, \gamma_{01}\) developed in Chapter~\ref{chap:Curves}
1167	(Definitions~\ref{def:P1_chartOpen}, \ref{def:P1_chartCoord},
1168	\ref{def:P1_chartSectionsEquiv0}--\ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}); the statements here
1169	are recorded in this chapter because they are private inputs of the finiteness glue rather
1170	than general theory of the projective line. Throughout, for a homogeneous \(f\) of positive
1171	degree we write \(A_{(f)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\) for the canonical map from the
1172	degree-zero localization to the sections over the basic open (an isomorphism).
1173	
1174	\begin{lemma}[Morphisms over the base intertwine the structure algebra maps]
1175	  \label{lem:appTop_map_appLE}
1176	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.appTop_map_appLE}
1177	  \leanok
1178	  Let \(k\) be a commutative ring, let \(X, Y\) be schemes over \(\Spec k\) and let
1179	  \(\pi : X \to Y\) be a morphism compatible with the structure morphisms. For opens
1180	  \(U \subseteq Y\) and \(V \subseteq X\) with \(V \subseteq \pi^{-1}(U)\), the two
1181	  composite ring homomorphisms
1182	  \[
1183	    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(Y, \top) \to \Gamma(Y, U)
1184	      \xrightarrow{\ \pi^\sharp\ } \Gamma(X, V)
1185	    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
1186	    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(X, \top) \to \Gamma(X, V)
1187	  \]
1188	  agree, where the unlabeled maps are induced by the structure morphisms and by
1189	  restriction.
1190	\end{lemma}
1191	\begin{proof}
1192	  \leanok
1193	  Pulling back sections along \(\pi\) commutes with restriction, so the first composite is
1194	  the map on sections induced by \(\pi\) composed with the structure morphism of \(Y\),
1195	  restricted to \(V\); by compatibility this composite of morphisms is the structure
1196	  morphism of \(X\).
1197	\end{proof}

1199	\begin{lemma}[Pulling back the structure algebra map]
1200	  \label{lem:appLE_overAlgebraMap}
1201	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.appLE_overAlgebraMap}
1202	  \uses{def:overAlgebraMap, lem:appTop_map_appLE}
1203	  \leanok
1204	  In the situation of \ref{lem:appTop_map_appLE}, for every \(r \in k\) the map
1205	  \(\pi^\sharp : \Gamma(Y, U) \to \Gamma(X, V)\) sends the image of \(r\) under the
1206	  structure algebra map of \(Y\) (Definition~\ref{def:overAlgebraMap}) to the image of
1207	  \(r\) under the structure algebra map of \(X\).
1208	\end{lemma}
1209	\begin{proof}
1210	  \leanok
1211	  Evaluate the equality of ring homomorphisms of \ref{lem:appTop_map_appLE} at the section
1212	  corresponding to \(r\).
1213	\end{proof}

1215	\begin{lemma}[The basic-open models lie over the base]
1216	  \label{lem:P1_awayi_structureMap}
1217	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.awayι_structureMap}
1218	  \uses{def:P1_structureMap}
1219	  \leanok
1220	  Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The composite of the affine
1221	  model \(\Spec A_{(f)} \to \PP^1\) of the basic open \(D_+(f)\) with the structure
1222	  morphism \(\PP^1 \to \Spec k\) is the morphism induced by the algebra map
1223	  \(k \to A_{(f)}\). (This generalizes \ref{lem:P1_chartIota_structureMap} from the two
1224	  standard charts to all standard basic opens.)
1225	\end{lemma}
1226	\begin{proof}
1227	  \leanok
1228	  \uses{def:P1_gradeZero}

1230	  \(\Proj A \to \Spec A_0\), restricted to the affine model of a basic open, is induced by
1231	  the ring homomorphism \(A_0 \to A_{(f)}\), and composing with the isomorphism
1232	  \(k \cong A_0\) of \ref{def:P1_gradeZero} gives the claim.
1233	\end{proof}

1235	\begin{lemma}[The basic-open inclusion factors through its affine model]
1236	  \label{lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq}
1237	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.basicOpen_ι_eq}
1238	  \uses{def:P1}
1239	  \leanok
1240	  Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The inclusion
1241	  \(D_+(f) \to \PP^1\) is the composite of the canonical identification
1242	  \(D_+(f) \cong \Spec A_{(f)}\) with the affine model \(\Spec A_{(f)} \to \PP^1\).
1243	\end{lemma}
1244	\begin{proof}
1245	  \leanok
1246	  The affine model is by construction an open immersion with image \(D_+(f)\), and the
1247	  canonical identification is the induced isomorphism onto the image; composing the two
1248	  recovers the inclusion.
1249	\end{proof}

1251	\begin{lemma}[The structure algebra map on a basic open]
1252	  \label{lem:P1_structureMap_appTop_awayToSection}
1253	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.structureMap_appTop_awayToSection}
1254	  \uses{def:P1_structureMap, lem:P1_awayi_structureMap, lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq}
1255	  \leanok
1256	  Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The composite
1257	  \[
1258	    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(\PP^1, \top) \to \Gamma\bigl(\PP^1, D_+(f)\bigr)
1259	  \]
1260	  (structure morphism on global sections, then restriction) is the composite of the
1261	  identification \(\Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \cong k\), the algebra map \(k \to A_{(f)}\), and
1262	  the canonical map \(A_{(f)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\).
1263	\end{lemma}
1264	\begin{proof}
1265	  \leanok
1266	  By \ref{lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq} and \ref{lem:P1_awayi_structureMap}, the composite of
1267	  the inclusion \(D_+(f) \to \PP^1\) with the structure morphism is the identification
1268	  \(D_+(f) \cong \Spec A_{(f)}\) followed by the morphism induced by \(k \to A_{(f)}\).
1269	  Taking global sections of this equality of scheme morphisms, and identifying the global
1270	  sections of the open subscheme \(D_+(f)\) with \(\Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\) --- under which
1271	  the map on sections induced by the identification with \(\Spec A_{(f)}\) becomes the
1272	  canonical map \(A_{(f)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\) --- yields the claim.
1273	\end{proof}
1274	
1275	\begin{lemma}[The distinguished fraction of a chart pair is the chart coordinate]
1276	  \label{lem:P1_isLocalizationElem_X_eq}
1277	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.isLocalizationElem_X_eq}
1278	  \uses{def:P1_chartCoord}
1279	  \leanok
1280	  For \(i, j \in \{0,1\}\), the canonical degree-zero fraction
1281	  \(X_j^{\deg X_i} / X_i^{\deg X_j}\) attached to the pair \((X_i, X_j)\) of homogeneous
1282	  elements equals the chart coordinate \(t_{ij} = X_j / X_i \in A_{(X_i)}\).
1283	\end{lemma}
1284	\begin{proof}
1285	  \leanok
1286	  Both degrees are one, and a first power is the element itself.
1287	\end{proof}

1289	\begin{theorem}[The chart coordinate cuts out the overlap]
1290	  \label{thm:P1_basicOpen_chartCoord}
1291	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord}
1292	  \uses{def:P1_chartOpen, def:P1_chartCoord, lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq,
1293	    lem:P1_isLocalizationElem_X_eq}
1294	  \leanok
1295	  For \(i, j \in \{0,1\}\), regard the chart coordinate \(t_{ij} \in A_{(X_i)}\) as a
1296	  section of the structure sheaf over the chart \(U_i = D_+(X_i)\), via the canonical map
1297	  \(A_{(X_i)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, U_i)\). Then the basic open of this section in the scheme
1298	  \(\PP^1\) --- the locus of \(U_i\) where it is invertible --- is the chart overlap:
1299	  \[
1300	    D(t_{ij}) \;=\; U_i \cap U_j .
1301	  \]
1302	\end{theorem}
1303	\begin{proof}
1304	  \leanok
1305	  Both sides are open subsets of \(U_i\) (the basic open of a section over \(U_i\) is
1306	  contained in \(U_i\)), so it suffices to show that they have the same preimage under the
1307	  identification \(U_i \cong \Spec A_{(X_i)}\), and to transport the equality forward
1308	  along this open immersion. No stalks are involved: everything is transported through
1309	  the affine model.
1310	
1311	  On the one hand, the preimage of the basic open \(D(t_{ij})\) is the basic open of
1312	  \(\Spec A_{(X_i)}\) at the ring element \(t_{ij}\): under the identification of an
1313	  affine open with the spectrum of its section ring, scheme-level basic opens of sections
1314	  correspond to spectrum-level basic opens of ring elements.
1315	
1316	  On the other hand, the preimage of \(U_j = D_+(X_j)\) under the affine model
1317	  \(\Spec A_{(X_i)} \to \PP^1\) (through which the inclusion of \(U_i\) factors,
1318	  \ref{lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq}) is the basic open at the canonical degree-zero fraction
1319	  attached to the pair \((X_i, X_j)\): a homogeneous prime avoiding \(X_i\) avoids
1320	  \(X_j\) exactly when the degree-zero fraction \(X_j/X_i\) is invertible in the
1321	  corresponding localization. By \ref{lem:P1_isLocalizationElem_X_eq} this fraction is
1322	  \(t_{ij}\), so the preimage of \(U_i \cap U_j\) is again the basic open at
1323	  \(t_{ij}\).
1324	\end{proof}

1326	\begin{lemma}[The Laurent generators as restrictions from the charts]
1327	  \label{lem:P1_laurent_generators}
1328	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T,
1329	    AlgebraicGeometry.P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T_neg,

1331	  \uses{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv, def:P1_chartCoord}
1332	  \leanok
1333	  Under the identification
1334	  \(\gamma_{01} : \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1) \cong k[T, T^{-1}]\) of
1335	  \ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}:
1336	  \begin{enumerate}
1337	    \item \(T\) corresponds to the restriction to the overlap of the chart coordinate
1338	      \(t_{01}\), regarded as a section over \(U_0\);
1339	    \item \(T^{-1}\) corresponds to the restriction to the overlap of the chart
1340	      coordinate \(t_{10}\), regarded as a section over \(U_1\);

1342	      the image of \(r\) under the algebra map \(k \to A_{(X_0X_1)}\).
1343	  \end{enumerate}
1344	\end{lemma}
1345	\begin{proof}

1347	  \uses{lem:P1_res_left, lem:P1_res_right}
1348	  (1) and (2): by \ref{lem:P1_res_left} (resp.\ \ref{lem:P1_res_right}), restriction from
1349	  the chart \(U_0\) (resp.\ \(U_1\)) to the overlap corresponds, under the
1350	  identifications \(\gamma_0, \gamma_1, \gamma_{01}\), to \(t \mapsto T\) (resp.\
1351	  \(t \mapsto T^{-1}\)); apply this to the sections corresponding to the polynomial
1352	  \(t\), which are the chart coordinates. (3): \(\gamma_{01}\) is built from the
1353	  \(k\)-algebra isomorphism \(\theta\) of \ref{def:P1_overlapAlgEquiv}, hence matches the
1354	  two algebra maps from \(k\).
1355	\end{proof}

1357	\section{Finiteness of the first cohomology}
1358	
1359	Combining the two-affine-cover cokernel bridge with the two-lattice ladder of
1360	Chapter~\ref{chap:Algebra} along a finite morphism to the projective line yields the
1361	finiteness of \(H^1\). Classically this computation goes back to the explicit \v{C}ech
1362	computation of the cohomology of projective space --- for \(\PP^1\) itself, the
1363	description of \(H^1\) as the cokernel of the two-chart restriction-difference map into
1364	the Laurent ring, spanned by the finitely many ``negative'' monomials --- extended to a
1365	curve by pushing forward along a finite morphism; the two-lattice ladder is exactly the
1366	abstraction of that monomial bookkeeping.
1367	
1368	\begin{theorem}[Finiteness of \(H^1\) along a finite morphism to the projective line]
1369	  \label{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}
1370	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}
1371	  \uses{def:HModule, def:moduleKSheaf, def:P1_structureMap}
1372	  \leanok
1373	  \source{hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0242, hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0243}
1374	  Let \(k\) be a field, \(X\) a scheme over \(\Spec k\), and \(\pi : X \to \PP^1\) a
1375	  finite morphism over \(k\) (its composite with the structure morphism of \(\PP^1\) is
1376	  the structure morphism of \(X\)). Then \(H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr)\) is a finite
1377	  \(k\)-module.
1378	\end{theorem}
1379	\begin{proof}
1380	  \leanok
1381	  \uses{lem:preimage_chart_affine, lem:preimage_chart_sup, lem:finite_app_overlap,
1382	    lem:P1_chartOpen_inf, thm:TwoCover_h1CokEquiv, def:TwoCover_diff, def:TwoCover_H1Cok,
1383	    def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv, def:P1_chartCoord, lem:P1_laurent_generators,
1384	    lem:appLE_overAlgebraMap, lem:P1_structureMap_appTop_awayToSection,
1385	    thm:P1_basicOpen_chartCoord, cor:two_lattice_loc_pow}
1386	  Write \(U_0, U_1\) for the standard charts of \(\PP^1\) and set
1387	  \(V_i = \pi^{-1}(U_i)\).
1388	
1389	  (a) \emph{The cover and the cokernel.} Since \(\pi\) is finite, hence affine, the
1390	  \(V_i\) are affine opens of \(X\) (\ref{lem:preimage_chart_affine}), and they cover
1391	  \(X\) (\ref{lem:preimage_chart_sup}). By the two-affine-cover bridge
1392	  \ref{thm:TwoCover_h1CokEquiv},
1393	  \[
1394	    H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr) \;\cong\;
1395	      N \big/ \mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff}),
1396	    \qquad N := \Gamma(X, V_0 \cap V_1),
1397	  \]
1398	  with \(\mathrm{diff}(s_0, s_1) = s_0|_{V_0 \cap V_1} - s_1|_{V_0 \cap V_1}\)
1399	  (\ref{def:TwoCover_diff}). It therefore suffices to prove that this quotient is a
1400	  finite \(k\)-module.
1401	
1402	  (b) \emph{The Laurent module structure.} Preimages commute with intersections, and
1403	  \(U_0 \cap U_1 = D_+(X_0X_1)\) (\ref{lem:P1_chartOpen_inf}), so
1404	  \(V_0 \cap V_1 = \pi^{-1}(U_0 \cap U_1)\). Make \(N\) an algebra over the Laurent
1405	  polynomial ring via the composite
1406	  \[
1407	    k[T, T^{-1}] \xrightarrow{\ \gamma_{01}^{-1}\ } \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1)
1408	      \xrightarrow{\ \pi^\sharp\ } \Gamma\bigl(X, \pi^{-1}(U_0 \cap U_1)\bigr) = N
1409	  \]
1410	  (\ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}). This structure is compatible with the \(k\)-module
1411	  structure of \(N\): a scalar \(r \in k[T,T^{-1}]\) corresponds under \(\gamma_{01}\) to
1412	  the image of \(r\) under the algebra map into the overlap ring
1413	  (\ref{lem:P1_laurent_generators}(3)), which is the structure algebra map of \(\PP^1\)
1414	  on \(U_0 \cap U_1\) (\ref{lem:P1_structureMap_appTop_awayToSection}), and \(\pi\) pulls
1415	  the structure algebra map of \(\PP^1\) back to that of \(X\)
1416	  (\ref{lem:appLE_overAlgebraMap}). Hence the \(k\)-module structure of \(N\) is the
1417	  restriction of scalars of the \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-structure along the canonical map
1418	  \(k \to k[T,T^{-1}]\).
1419	
1420	  (c) \emph{Module-finiteness over the Laurent ring.} Since \(\pi\) is finite and
1421	  \(U_0 \cap U_1\) is an affine open of \(\PP^1\), the map
1422	  \(\pi^\sharp : \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1) \to N\) is module-finite
1423	  (\ref{lem:finite_app_overlap}); composing with the isomorphism \(\gamma_{01}^{-1}\),
1424	  \(N\) is a finite \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-module.
1425	
1426	  (d) \emph{The two lattices, and the range of the difference map.} Let
1427	  \(Q_0, Q_1 \subseteq N\) be the images of the (\(k\)-linear) restriction maps
1428	  \(\Gamma(X, V_0) \to N\) and \(\Gamma(X, V_1) \to N\). Then
1429	  \(\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff}) = Q_0 + Q_1\): every value
1430	  \(s_0| - s_1|\) of \(\mathrm{diff}\) is the sum of \(s_0| \in Q_0\) and
1431	  \(-(s_1|) = (-s_1)| \in Q_1\); conversely \(s_0| = \mathrm{diff}(s_0, 0) \) and
1432	  \(s_1| = \mathrm{diff}(0, -s_1)\) exhibit every element of \(Q_0\) and of \(Q_1\) as a
1433	  value of \(\mathrm{diff}\) --- the sign is absorbed because \(Q_1\) is the image of a
1434	  linear map.
1435	
1436	  (e) \emph{Lattice stability.} Let
1437	  \(\tau_0 = \pi^\sharp(t_{01}) \in \Gamma(X, V_0)\) and
1438	  \(\tau_1 = \pi^\sharp(t_{10}) \in \Gamma(X, V_1)\) be the pullbacks of the chart
1439	  coordinates, regarded as sections over the charts
1440	  (Definition~\ref{def:P1_chartCoord}). By \ref{lem:P1_laurent_generators}(1) and the
1441	  compatibility of \(\pi^\sharp\) with restriction, \(T\) acts on \(N\) as
1442	  multiplication by \(\tau_0|_{V_0 \cap V_1}\); symmetrically \(T^{-1}\) acts as
1443	  multiplication by \(\tau_1|_{V_0 \cap V_1}\) (\ref{lem:P1_laurent_generators}(2)).
1444	  Hence \(Q_0\) is stable under multiplication by \(T\): for \(s \in \Gamma(X, V_0)\),
1445	  \[
1446	    T \cdot s|_{V_0 \cap V_1} \;=\; \tau_0|\cdot s| \;=\; (\tau_0 s)|_{V_0 \cap V_1}
1447	      \;\in\; Q_0,
1448	  \]
1449	  and symmetrically \(Q_1\) is stable under multiplication by \(T^{-1}\).
1450	
1451	  (f) \emph{Absorption up to powers.} The overlap is a basic open inside each chart
1452	  preimage: pulling back the identity \(D(t_{ij}) = U_i \cap U_j\) of
1453	  \ref{thm:P1_basicOpen_chartCoord} along \(\pi\) (basic opens of sections pull back to
1454	  basic opens of the pulled-back sections) gives
1455	  \[
1456	    V_0 \cap V_1 = D(\tau_0) \subseteq V_0,
1457	    \qquad
1458	    V_0 \cap V_1 = D(\tau_1) \subseteq V_1 .
1459	  \]
1460	  Since \(V_0\) is affine and \(V_0 \cap V_1\) is its basic open defined by \(\tau_0\),
1461	  restriction identifies \(N\) with the localization of \(\Gamma(X, V_0)\) at the powers
1462	  of \(\tau_0\) (quasi-coherence of the structure sheaf). Hence for every \(n \in N\)
1463	  there are \(m \ge 0\) and \(a \in \Gamma(X, V_0)\) with
1464	  \(n \cdot (\tau_0|)^m = a|\), i.e.\ \(T^m \cdot n \in Q_0\). Symmetrically, every
1465	  \(n \in N\) satisfies \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\) for some \(m \ge 0\).
1466	
1467	  (g) \emph{The ladder.} By (b), (c), (e) and (f), the module \(N\) over

11	# Finiteness of `H¹(X, 𝒪_X)` via a finite morphism to the projective line
12	
13	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` equipped with a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, this
14	file proves that the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf of `X` (as a sheaf of
15	`k`-modules on the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) is a finite `k`-module — and derives
16	the instance for the smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve of the challenge, so that
17	`genus` is the dimension of an honestly finite-dimensional vector space.
18	
19	The proof is the *two-lattice ladder* of `AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.TwoLattice` run on the
20	Mayer–Vietoris cokernel of `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.TwoCover`:
21	
22	* `V i := π ⁻¹ᵁ D₊(Xᵢ)` is an affine open cover of `X`
23	  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), so
24	  `H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁) ⧸ range (res₀ - res₁)` (`TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`);
25	* `N := Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)` is a module over the Laurent polynomial ring `k[T;T⁻¹]` through
26	  `π`'s map on sections over the chart overlap and the identification
27	  `Γ(ℙ¹, D₊(X₀X₁)) ≃ k[T,T⁻¹]` (`P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`); it is module-finite because `π`
28	  is finite (`finite_app_overlap`);
29	* `Q₀, Q₁ :=` the images of `Γ(V₀), Γ(V₁)` in `N` are `k`-submodules with
30	  `range (res₀ - res₁) = Q₀ ⊔ Q₁`; `Q₀` is stable under `T` because `T` is the restriction
31	  of the chart-0 coordinate, which extends to `V₀` (symmetrically for `Q₁` and `T⁻¹`); and
32	  `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is the basic open of the pulled-back chart coordinate inside the affine `V₀`
33	  (`P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord`), so
34	  `IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_of_eq_basicOpen` provides the surjectivity-up-to-powers
35	  hypotheses of the two-lattice lemma.
36	
37	The `ℙ¹`-side identifications live in `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.FinitenessP1`.
38	
39	## Main declarations
40	
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1` — **the conditional
42	  finiteness theorem**: if `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹` is finite with `π ≫ P1.structureMap k = X ↘ Spec k`,
43	  then `Module.Finite k (H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪_X))`.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one` — the instance for the challenge curve
45	  `C` (smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible over `k`), consuming
46	  `exists_isFinite_toP1`; it is keyed on exactly the `letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k))`
47	  spelling used by `genus` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Challenge`.

50	(`FiniteDimensional` is an abbreviation for `Module.Finite`), so no separate corollary is
51	needed.
52	-/

/-!

# `CartesianMonoidalCategory` for `Over X`

We provide a `CartesianMonoidalCategory (Over X)` instance via pullbacks, and provide simp lemmas
for the induced `MonoidalCategory (Over X)` instance.

-/

public noncomputable section

namespace CategoryTheory.Over

open Functor Limits CartesianMonoidalCategory

variable {C : Type*} [Category* C] [HasPullbacks C]

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
/-- A choice of finite products of `Over X` given by `Limits.pullback`. -/
abbrev cartesianMonoidalCategory (X : C) : CartesianMonoidalCategory (Over X) :=
  .ofChosenFiniteProducts
    ⟨asEmptyCone (Over.mk (𝟙 X)), IsTerminal.ofUniqueHom (fun Y ↦ Over.homMk Y.hom)
      fun Y m ↦ Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simpa using m.w)⟩
    fun Y Z ↦ ⟨pullbackConeEquivBinaryFan.functor.obj (pullback.cone Y.hom Z.hom),
    (pullback.isLimit _ _).pullbackConeEquivBinaryFanFunctor⟩

attribute [local instance] cartesianMonoidalCategory

/-- `Over X` is braided w.r.t. the Cartesian monoidal structure given by `Limits.pullback`. -/
abbrev braidedCategory (X : C) : BraidedCategory (Over X) :=
  .ofCartesianMonoidalCategory

attribute [local instance] braidedCategory

open MonoidalCategory

variable {X : C}

@[ext]
lemma tensorObj_ext {R : C} {S T : Over X} (f₁ f₂ : R ⟶ (S ⊗ T).left)
    (e₁ : f₁ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = f₂ ≫ pullback.fst _ _)
    (e₂ : f₁ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = f₂ ≫ pullback.snd _ _) : f₁ = f₂ :=
  pullback.hom_ext e₁ e₂

@[simp]
lemma tensorObj_left (R S : Over X) : (R ⊗ S).left = Limits.pullback R.hom S.hom := rfl

@[simp]
lemma tensorObj_hom (R S : Over X) : (R ⊗ S).hom = pullback.fst R.hom S.hom ≫ R.hom := rfl

@[simp]
lemma tensorUnit_left : (𝟙_ (Over X)).left = X := rfl

@[simp]
lemma tensorUnit_hom : (𝟙_ (Over X)).hom = 𝟙 X := rfl

@[simp]
lemma lift_left {R S T : Over X} (f : R ⟶ S) (g : R ⟶ T) :
    (lift f g).left = pullback.lift f.left g.left (f.w.trans g.w.symm) := rfl

@[simp]
lemma fst_left {R S : Over X} : (fst R S).left = pullback.fst _ _ := rfl

@[simp]
lemma snd_left {R S : Over X} : (snd R S).left = pullback.snd _ _ := rfl

@[simp]
lemma toUnit_left {R : Over X} : (toUnit R).left = R.hom := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_hom_left_fst (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).hom.left ≫ pullback.fst _ (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) =
      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_hom_left_snd_fst (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).hom.left ≫ pullback.snd _ (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π_assoc _ _ _).trans (limit.lift_π _ _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_hom_left_snd_snd (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).hom.left ≫ pullback.snd _ (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
      pullback.snd _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π_assoc _ _ _).trans (limit.lift_π _ _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_inv_left_fst_fst (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
      pullback.fst _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π_assoc _ _ _).trans (limit.lift_π _ _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_inv_left_fst_snd (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
      pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π_assoc _ _ _).trans (limit.lift_π _ _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_inv_left_snd (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).inv.left ≫ pullback.snd (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) _ =
      pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[simp]
lemma leftUnitor_hom_left (Y : Over X) :
    (λ_ Y).hom.left = pullback.snd _ _ := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma leftUnitor_inv_left_fst (Y : Over X) :
    (λ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst (𝟙 X) _ = Y.hom :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma leftUnitor_inv_left_snd (Y : Over X) :
    (λ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.snd (𝟙 X) _ = 𝟙 Y.left :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[simp]
lemma rightUnitor_hom_left (Y : Over X) :
    (ρ_ Y).hom.left = pullback.fst _ (𝟙 X) := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma rightUnitor_inv_left_fst (Y : Over X) :
    (ρ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst _ (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 _ :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma rightUnitor_inv_left_snd (Y : Over X) :
    (ρ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.snd _ (𝟙 X) = Y.hom :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

lemma whiskerLeft_left {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (R ◁ f).left = pullback.map _ _ _ _ (𝟙 _) f.left (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp) := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma whiskerLeft_left_fst {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (R ◁ f).left ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = pullback.fst _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π _ _).trans (Category.comp_id _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma whiskerLeft_left_snd {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (R ◁ f).left ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = pullback.snd _ _ ≫ f.left :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

lemma whiskerRight_left {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (f ▷ R).left = pullback.map _ _ _ _ f.left (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp) := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma whiskerRight_left_fst {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (f ▷ R).left ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = pullback.fst _ _ ≫ f.left :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma whiskerRight_left_snd {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (f ▷ R).left ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = pullback.snd _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π _ _).trans (Category.comp_id _)

lemma tensorHom_left {R S T U : Over X} (f : R ⟶ S) (g : T ⟶ U) :
    (f ⊗ₘ g).left = pullback.map _ _ _ _ f.left g.left (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp) := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma tensorHom_left_fst {S U : C} {R T : Over X} (fS : S ⟶ X) (fU : U ⟶ X)
    (f : R ⟶ mk fS) (g : T ⟶ mk fU) :
    (f ⊗ₘ g).left ≫ pullback.fst fS fU = pullback.fst R.hom T.hom ≫ f.left :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma tensorHom_left_snd {S U : C} {R T : Over X} (fS : S ⟶ X) (fU : U ⟶ X)
    (f : R ⟶ mk fS) (g : T ⟶ mk fU) :
    (f ⊗ₘ g).left ≫ pullback.snd fS fU = pullback.snd R.hom T.hom ≫ g.left :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[simp]
lemma braiding_hom_left {R S : Over X} :
    (β_ R S).hom.left = (pullbackSymmetry _ _).hom := rfl

@[simp]
lemma braiding_inv_left {R S : Over X} :
    (β_ R S).inv.left = (pullbackSymmetry _ _).hom := rfl

variable {A B R S Y Z : C} {f : R ⟶ X} {g : S ⟶ X}

instance : (Over.pullback f).Braided := .ofChosenFiniteProducts _

@[simp]
lemma η_pullback_left : (OplaxMonoidal.η (Over.pullback f)).left = (pullback.snd (𝟙 _) f) := rfl

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
@[simp]
lemma ε_pullback_left : (LaxMonoidal.ε (Over.pullback f)).left = inv (pullback.snd (𝟙 _) f) := by
  apply IsIso.eq_inv_of_hom_inv_id
  rw [← η_pullback_left, ← Over.comp_left, Monoidal.η_ε, Over.id_left]

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
lemma μ_pullback_left_fst_fst (R S : Over X) :
    (LaxMonoidal.μ (Over.pullback f) R S).left ≫
      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ := by
  rw [Monoidal.μ_of_cartesianMonoidalCategory,
    ← cancel_epi (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) R S).hom.left, ← Over.comp_left_assoc,
    Iso.hom_inv_id]
  simp [CartesianMonoidalCategory.prodComparison, fst]

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
lemma μ_pullback_left_fst_snd (R S : Over X) :
    (LaxMonoidal.μ (Over.pullback f) R S).left ≫
      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ := by
  rw [Monoidal.μ_of_cartesianMonoidalCategory,
    ← cancel_epi (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) R S).hom.left,
    ← Over.comp_left_assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id]
  simp [CartesianMonoidalCategory.prodComparison, snd]

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
lemma μ_pullback_left_snd (R S : Over X) :
    (LaxMonoidal.μ (Over.pullback f) R S).left ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
      pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ := by
  rw [Monoidal.μ_of_cartesianMonoidalCategory,
    ← cancel_epi (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) R S).hom.left,
    ← Over.comp_left_assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id]
  simp [CartesianMonoidalCategory.prodComparison]

lemma μ_pullback_left_fst_fst' (g₁ : Y ⟶ X) (g₂ : Z ⟶ X) :
    (LaxMonoidal.μ (Over.pullback f) (.mk g₁) (.mk g₂)).left ≫
      pullback.fst (pullback.fst g₁ g₂ ≫ g₁) f ≫ pullback.fst g₁ g₂ =
        pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ :=
  μ_pullback_left_fst_fst ..

@[simp]
lemma μ_pullback_left_fst_snd' (g₁ : Y ⟶ X) (g₂ : Z ⟶ X) :
    (LaxMonoidal.μ (Over.pullback f) (.mk g₁) (.mk g₂)).left ≫
      pullback.fst (pullback.fst g₁ g₂ ≫ g₁) f ≫ pullback.snd g₁ g₂ =
        pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ :=
  μ_pullback_left_fst_snd ..

lemma μ_pullback_left_snd' (g₁ : Y ⟶ X) (g₂ : Z ⟶ X) :
    (LaxMonoidal.μ (Over.pullback f) (.mk g₁) (.mk g₂)).left ≫
      pullback.snd (pullback.fst g₁ g₂ ≫ g₁) f =
        pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ := μ_pullback_left_snd ..

@[simp]
lemma preservesTerminalIso_pullback (f : R ⟶ S) :
    preservesTerminalIso (Over.pullback f) =
      Over.isoMk (asIso (pullback.snd (𝟙 _) f)) (by simp) := by
  ext1; exact toUnit_unique _ _

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
@[simp]
lemma prodComparisonIso_pullback_inv_left_fst_fst (f : X ⟶ Y) (A B : Over Y) :
    (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) A B).inv.left ≫
      pullback.fst (pullback.fst A.hom B.hom ≫ A.hom) f ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
        pullback.fst (pullback.snd A.hom f) (pullback.snd B.hom f) ≫ pullback.fst _ _ := by

    Over.hom_left_inv_left_assoc]

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
@[simp]
lemma prodComparisonIso_pullback_inv_left_fst_snd' (f : X ⟶ Y) (gA : A ⟶ Y) (gB : B ⟶ Y) :

lemma prodComparisonIso_pullback_inv_left_snd' (f : X ⟶ Y) (gA : A ⟶ Y) (gB : B ⟶ Y) :

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in

10	
11	In this section we make explicit calculations of the cohomology of the
12	sheaves $\mathcal{O}(n)$ on a projective space, by using \v{C}ech cohomology
13	for a suitable open affine covering. These explicit calculations form the
14	basis for various general results about cohomology of coherent sheaves on
15	projective varieties.
16	
17	Let $A$ be a noetherian ring, let $S = A[x_0, \ldots, x_r]$, and let
18	$X = \Proj S$ be the projective space $\mathbf{P}^r_A$ over $A$. Let
19	$\mathcal{O}_X(1)$ be the twisting sheaf of Serre (II, \S 5). For any sheaf
20	of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $\mathcal{F}$, we denote by $\Gamma_*(\mathcal{F})$
21	the graded $S$-module $\bigoplus_{n \in \mathbf{Z}} \Gamma(X, \mathcal{F}(n))$
22	(see II, \S 5).

24	\begin{theorem}[5.1]
25	Let $A$ be a noetherian ring, and let $X = \mathbf{P}^r_A$, with $r \ge 1$.
26	Then:
27	\begin{enumerate}
28	\item[(a)] the natural map $S \to \Gamma_*(\mathcal{O}_X) =
29	  \bigoplus_{n \in \mathbf{Z}} H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(n))$ is an isomorphism of
30	  graded $S$-modules;
31	\item[(b)] $H^i(X, \mathcal{O}_X(n)) = 0$ for $0 < i < r$ and all
32	  $n \in \mathbf{Z}$;
33	\item[(c)] $H^r(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-r-1)) \cong A$;

13	   `Sheaf.HModule F n` of a sheaf `F` of `R`-modules, defined as the `Ext`-group from the

15	   `AddCommGrpCat`-valued; ours is `ModuleCat R`-valued so that `Module.finrank` applies).

17	   category, and `Sheaf.HModule.map` gives `R`-linear functoriality in `F`.

21	   `Scheme.moduleKSheaf` on the small Zariski site `Opens.grothendieckTopology X`, by
22	   restriction of scalars along the structure morphism, with definitional (`rfl`) access

26	
27	Everything is single-universe: `k : Type u`, `X : Scheme.{u}`, the site `Opens X : Type u`
